title: The cave and the road
hook: The trackers stood at the cave's mouth. One sentence kept two hunted men calm: Allah is with us.

screens.text: **The trackers were standing at the mouth of the cave.** Abu Bakr said that if they only looked down at their feet, they'd see them. The Prophet ﷺ answered him: what do you think of two, when Allah is their third? [Bukhari 3653]
**Three nights in a cave.** They hid in the cave of Thawr, on a mountain outside Makkah. Abu Bakr's son came each night with news from the city [Bukhari 3905; IslamQA 10063].

screens.text: **A rider and a reward.** Quraysh offered a large reward for them. A rider named Suraqah ibn Malik caught up, but his horse's legs sank into the ground, more than once. He asked for safety, and they wrote him a promise of it [Bukhari 3906].
bubbles: That morning he was hunting them. By the end of the day he was steering others away from them [Bukhari 3911]. Years later he became Muslim, the early sources report [IslamQA 11575].

screens.prompt: Suraqah had chased them to hand them over. When he asked for safety, what did they do?

options.text: Gave him a written promise of safety
options.feedback: Right. The hunter left protected by the people he was hunting [Bukhari 3906].

options.text: Took his horse and left him in the desert
options.feedback: Not quite. They gave him what he asked for: a written promise of safety.

options.text: Made him swear to join them
options.feedback: Not quite. No pressure. He became Muslim years later, by his own choice.

screens.text: **A lifeline for anyone who feels alone.** If you're hiding your faith at home, praying in a car, or feeling like everyone's watching you, the words from the cave are for you too. Allah is with you, in the tightest spot.
bubbles: Day 43 said it too: what Allah has written for you, no one can take [Tirmidhi 2516]. Do your part, then rest in that: **tawakkul**.

screens.situation: Destiny hasn't told her roommates she's Muslim. She prays quietly in her room with the door locked, and her heart pounds every time someone walks past. Tonight she feels completely alone.

options.text: Pray anyway, remind herself Allah is with her, and message her mentor about next steps
options.feedback: Yes. Calm effort plus trust. Two in a cave weren't alone, and neither is she.

options.text: Stop praying until she's ready to tell them
options.feedback: Not quite. She can pray quietly and privately now. Telling people can wait for the right time.

options.text: Tell everyone tonight so she doesn't have to hide
options.feedback: Not quite. There's no rush. The Prophet ﷺ planned carefully too. Her mentor can help her choose the time.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- They hid three nights in the cave of Thawr. Abu Bakr's son 'Abdullah brought news each night, and 'Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Abu Bakr's freed slave, brought sheep near the cave after dark so they had milk [Bukhari 3905; IslamQA 10063].
- Abu Bakr feared the trackers would see them; the Prophet ﷺ asked what he thought of two whose third is Allah [Bukhari 3653]. The Qur'an: "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us" [Q 9:40].
- Their guide then led them along the coast [Bukhari 3905].
- Quraysh offered a large reward (IslamQA 11575 says two hundred camels; Bukhari 3906 says each one's blood-money). Suraqah ibn Malik caught up; his horse's legs sank more than once; he asked for safety and was given it in writing [Bukhari 3906; IslamQA 11575].
- Another narration: in the first part of the day Suraqah was chasing them, and by the end of it he was protecting them, keeping others off their trail [Bukhari 3911].
- Suraqah later became Muslim (IslamQA 11575: after the conquest of Makkah).

**Likely questions**
- *"Was there a spider web and a dove's nest at the cave?"* It's a well-known story whose chain scholars differ on (some graded the spider report acceptable, others weak), and the doves are weaker still [IslamQA 27224]. What's certain is the Qur'an's "Allah is with us." (scholar question Q43)
- *"Did angels cover the cave?"* That report is weak [IslamQA 27224]. Q 9:40 says Allah supported him with soldiers you did not see; leave the details there.
- *"Was 'Amir a slave?"* He had been enslaved and was freed (he's called Abu Bakr's freed slave in the hadith). Slavery existed everywhere then; questions beyond this go to the imam.
- *"I'm hiding my faith. How do I cope?"* Listen first. Private worship is fine; there's no deadline for telling people. Link to the mentor. If they're in any danger, the safety rule applies.

**Escalate:** any danger at home (safety rule first); detailed questions about slavery.

**Don't**
- Don't tell the spider, dove or angels-covering-the-cave stories as fact.
- Don't describe the Prophet's ﷺ appearance (Umm Ma'bad's description is outside the six collections and is left out).
- Don't push a convert to "come out" about their faith.
